content.title: About
content.content: Carrots are root vegetables belonging to the Apiaceae family. Raw carrots are commonly used in salads; they are crunchy, mildly sweet, and rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots were domesticated in Central Asia over 5,000 years ago.
Originally carrots were purple; the orange variety was developed in the 17th century in the Netherlands.
Raw carrots are more than 90 % water and contain virtually no fat.
Beta‑carotene from carrots can improve night vision.
Carrots can be used as a natural food coloring.

items.title: Rich source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene in carrots is converted to vitamin A, supporting eye health and immune function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Carrots contain antioxidants (carotenoids, vitamin C) that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in raw carrots promotes regular bowel movements and overall digestive health.

items.title: May reduce cardiovascular risk
items.content: Potassium and antioxidants help maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Vitamin A and antioxidants contribute to healthy skin and its regeneration.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to carrots.

items.title: Digestive discomfort with excess intake
items.content: Large amounts of raw carrot can cause gas and bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic carrots, rinse them thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw carrots can be cut into sticks, grated, or sliced into rounds for salads, snacks, and smoothies. They work well in vegetable mixes or as dippers for hummus and other spreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store carrots in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, preferably in a perforated bag. When kept properly, they stay fresh for 2–3 weeks. Discard carrots that become soft, develop spots, or emit an off‑odor.
